text:
The scoreboard said New York pulled away, but the third period is where the game was actually won. The Rangers generated 2.26 expected goals in those final 20 minutes, nearly double what Utah managed (1.28), after the first two periods had been close to even. Over the full game the chance quality was tight enough that NYR deserved to win only 53 percent of the time, so this was a game that could have gone either way until the last period tilted it.

Vladislav Gavrikov opened the scoring late in the first on a wrist shot that had only a 2 percent chance of going in, and he added an assist on J.T. Miller's deflection that made it 3-1. Utah answered on the power play when Nick Schmaltz scored on a backhand in the second, then cut it to 2-3 on Andrew Peeke's snap shot with five minutes left. Gabe Perreault restored the lead early in the third, and Eeli Tolvanen sealed it at 18:45 with a 40 percent chance, the best look of the night, for the 4-2 final.

Utah actually outshot the Rangers in attempts, 69 to 55, and went 0 for 4 with a man advantage on the other side of its single power-play goal. Igor Shesterkin stopped 28 of 30 shots against 3.57 expected goals against, worth about 1.6 saves above expected, and he picked up an assist on Tolvanen's empty-net-sealing goal. Karel Vejmelka was solid too, but he gave up three goals on a lighter workload of 21 shots.
